description: EPATADA provides the US Environmental Protection Agency's Tools for Automated Data Analysis as an R package. It helps compile and evaluate samples from the Water Quality Portal and supports a separate TADAShiny application. Users select monitoring records, apply the documented preparation and quality-checking workflows and obtain data suitable for further analysis. Coverage follows participating US water-quality monitoring sources, with sampling dates and spatial density varying by site, not following a uniform grid. Public code, function references and example workflows are available free under CC0-1.0 as stated in GitHub licence metadata. The README marks the package experimental and recommends updating it and its dependencies before use. It also warns that the hosted Shiny version can lag the source release and can time out on large datasets. These limits matter for reproducible preparation. The package can prepare observations for water-quality model calibration, complementing the catalogue's HAWQS platform (platform-hawqs-hydrologic-water-quality-system). No monitoring data were retrieved and no claim of direct HAWQS format compatibility is made.
